facts.text: Pittsburgh was named in 1758 by General John Forbes after British statesman William Pitt, 1st Earl of Chatham.
The city’s film scene, once dormant, now hosts major productions like Disney and Paramount, thanks to a historic sound stage outside Los Angeles.
Carnegie Mellon University, founded by industrialists Andrew Carnegie and Andrew Mellon, remains a leading research university in Pittsburgh.
Carnegie’s Union Railroad, started in 1894, still ferries heavy freight for Pittsburgh’s steel industry, a legacy of George Westinghouse’s rail innovations.
